Subject: MeridianX inference deep-dive & next steps (latency/throughput SLOs)

Hi Alex + Priya,

Thanks again for the call today — great to get a clear line-of-sight into MeridianX's inference needs for the new personalization pipeline. Below is a concise recap and proposed next steps so we can align engineering and procurement.

High-level goals we captured:
- Real-time personalization API for web + mobile with P95 latency target of <= 150ms (target 120ms) for single-turn prompts up to 512 tokens.
- Peak throughput target ~350 requests/s during business hours, baseline sustained ~120 req/s.
- Model quality: want ~human-like fluency for summarization + classification; open to quantized 70B-class models if latency/cost checks out.
- Security/compliance: VPC + SOC2 evidence; customer-managed KMS required for Private deployment.

Key pain points discussed:
- Current vendor has unpredictable tail latency under burst traffic and opaque cost spikes.
- Need for a unified deployment that can fall back gracefully (lower-cost model variant) when Dedicated capacity is constrained.
- Hard requirement to preserve session KV across short-lived user interactions (approx 30s TTL).

Technical notes from the call (engineering items):
- Expected average sequence length: 120 tokens; 99th percentile sequence length ~420 tokens (worst-case admin queries).
- KV cache retention: up to 500k tokens/day per shard; we discussed prefix caching to reduce repeated context cost.
- Suggested runtime: Dedicated GPU pool (A10G/80GB-class for initial pilot) with autoscale to burst capacity; fallback routing to hosted smaller-quantized variant (e.g., 13B int8) for non-critical requests.
- Batching: target micro-batching window 20ms, batch size cap 8 for latency SLOs.

Proposed immediate next steps:
1) Camila to share the QPS/latency spreadsheet from today's load projection (attached).
2) Jonas to draft an initial topology sketch and ops runbook for a Dedicated + fallback hosted configuration by EOD Thu.
3) MeridianX to confirm security contacts and provide SOC2 auditor name (Priya to share).
4) Schedule a short infra walkthrough with MeridianX infra team (30 min) next week to validate VPC/KMS expectations.

Attachments: meridianx-mvp-qps-latency.xlsx (spreadsheet), redwood-deploy-topology-sketch.pdf (topology sketch).

If this recap looks right, please reply with any edits and confirm the earliest window for the infra walkthrough — aiming for Tue/Wed next week.

Best,

Camila,

Thanks for the thorough recap — that matches our notes. Couple quick clarifications from our side:
- P95 target: 120ms is preferred in the US West region; we can accept a higher P95 (up to 180ms) for non-customer-facing batch jobs.
- Throughput: 350 req/s peak is our conservative estimate; there may be short spikes to ~500 req/s for 2–3 minutes after marketing pushes.
- Model: preference is to evaluate a quantized 70B variant for quality comparison, but production can start on a 13B int8 variant if latency requires it.

Priya will send the SOC2 auditor contact by EOD today. We are available for an infra walkthrough on Wed (16 Jul) 10:00–10:30 PT — let us know if that works.

Thanks, Camila + Alex — good alignment. Quick engineering readout and assumptions I'm tracking: 

Assumptions:
- Target region: us-west2 (we'll benchmark there first).
- Model candidates for evaluation: LlamaX-70B-qat-int8 (quality candidate) and LlamaX-13B-int8 (latency candidate).
- Hardware baseline for pilot: 2 x A10G (80GB) + small NFS for logs; Dedicated pool sized for sustained 150 req/s, with autoscale to 4 A10G for burst windows.

Preliminary topology choices:
- API tier (edge LB) -> routing policy (latency-first for customer traffic; cost-first for internal batch) -> Dedicated pool (primary) with fallback routing to Redwood-hosted small-quant model.
- Prefix/KV caching at the serving runtime with 30s TTL for session-level caching; fallbacks will not rely on cached KV to avoid stale context.
- Batching strategy: 20ms window, max batch 8, dynamic schedule if queue > 100ms to prioritize tail latencies.

Open engineering questions for the infra walkthrough:
1) MeridianX expected concurrency distribution over minutes and peak burst patterns (Alex to confirm).
2) KMS integration flow (Priya to confirm whether HSM-backed KMS or cloud KMS).
3) Whether MeridianX requires on-prem or VPC-private control plane for the pilot.

I'll take point on drafting an ops runbook + topology sketch and upload to the shared Drive; Camila, I've added the sketch to the Drive link in the thread. Will aim for a first draft by Thu EOD.

-Jonas
